changes_made.explanation: Normalized task name to standard format. All extracted items were confirmed to be correct and relevant to NLG (Text-to-Speech).

Removed N-CMOS as it is a subjective/comparative metric (Comparative Mean Opinion Score), not an automatic metric. WER (Word Error Rate), SIM (Speaker Similarity), and UT-MOS (Universal Tag MOS) are valid automatic metrics used to evaluate the generated speech.
The paper does not use LLMs as judges/evaluators after generation. DeepSeek-V3 is used during dataset construction for text preprocessing and perturbation, not for evaluating generated outputs.

guideline: Subjects performed binary classification for reading accuracy (determining if speech accurately reads text without insertion/omission/mispronunciation)
Used Comparative Mean Opinion Score (N-CMOS rated from -2 to 2) for naturalness
Conducted A/B testing to compare speaker similarity between samples before and after alignment

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated criteria to their base forms (intelligibility, naturalness, speaker similarity) rather than including the specific evaluation method names. The guideline descriptions capture the specific evaluation procedures used.

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper focuses on Text-to-Speech intelligibility evaluation using both automatic metrics (WER, SIM, UT-MOS) and human evaluations (reading accuracy, CMOS, A/B tests). No LLM-as-judge evaluation was conducted. All metadata items were properly extracted and relevant to the respective questions.
